subject: TTFT + streaming SLOs — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme-ai.com>, Elizabeth Tan <e.tan@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: TTFT + streaming SLOs — follow-up & next steps

Hi Samir / Elizabeth —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on performance requirements for the PoC: 

Recap of what you told us:
- Primary UX: streaming token-by-token customer-facing chat (web app).
- TTFT expectations: p50 around 150ms, p95 under 400ms for 1–2 token first-chunk delivery.
- Typical request payload: ~150 tokens prompt, expected generation up to 512 tokens.
- Steady-state throughput: ~50 req/s, expected bursts up to 200 req/s.
- Concurrent streaming sessions at peak: ~300 (mostly long-lived connections, average duration ~30–90s).
- Preferred transport: WebSocket (you mentioned this is what the client uses today).

Clarifying questions / asks for PoC scope:
1) Can you confirm whether the p95 TTFT target is strict for peak bursts or for steady-state throughput? (We usually size differently for sustained vs. burst.)
2) For streaming chunk cadence: do you expect the first byte/token within the TTFT target and then subsequent chunks every ~100ms, or would larger chunk sizes (~200–300ms cadence) be acceptable?
3) Any hard constraints on network egress or VPC peering that would affect placement?

What we will deliver for the PoC:
- A scoped throughput test focused on TTFT (p50/p95) and sustained throughput at your target concurrency.
- Streaming via WebSocket endpoint matching your chunk cadence (we’ll prototype both 100ms and 250ms cadence).
- A short report with recommended instance sizing, batching configuration, and expected unit costs.

Next steps:
- I’ve attached a short proposal with a recommended test plan and timeline (acme-ttft-proposal.pdf).
- Please share the detailed requirements spreadsheet you mentioned (or confirm the numbers above).
- If everything looks good, propose a PoC kickoff window next week — suggest Thu 2/17 or Fri 2/18 PST.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa and Dev to scope engineering details once you confirm.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme-ttft-proposal.pdf (1 page — outline of PoC test plan and timeline)

From: Samir Shah <samir@acme-ai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elizabeth Tan <e.tan@acme-ai.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT + streaming SLOs — follow-up & next steps

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming answers below: 

- The p95 TTFT target is for customer-facing peak traffic — i.e., we expect it to hold during bursts up to 200 req/s. If you can size differently for sustained 50 req/s that’s fine but target is peak.
- WebSocket is the preferred transport. We need first token within the TTFT window, then we expect approx ~100ms cadence for subsequent chunks for a responsive experience. We can tolerate up to 200–250ms but prefer 100ms if possible.
- Concurrency: peak ~300 concurrent streaming sessions. Average session length ~45s.
- No unusual egress restrictions; we’ll share the network diagram if needed.

I’ve attached the detailed requirements workbook (acme-requirements.xlsx). The key ask: can you run a PoC that demonstrates p95 TTFT < 400ms under a 200 req/s burst with 300 concurrent streams?

We’re available for kickoff Fri 2/18 at 10:00 AM PST. Please confirm and send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform
Acme AI

Attachment: acme-requirements.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Feb 2028 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT + streaming SLOs — follow-up & next steps

Aditya —

Thanks — good summary. Internal notes / immediate actions: 
- I’ll spin up a brief engineering sync with Dev and Solutions Eng to map test harness for WebSocket streaming (we’ll validate both 100ms and 250ms chunk cadence).
- Dev: can you prepare a rough capacity estimate (GPU instance types, batch settings, and expected p95 TTFT at 200 req/s bursts) by EOD Thu? Include any suggestions on prefix caching and KV cache behavior for long sessions.
- I’ll draft the PoC plan and timeline and share for review.

Also included a short checklist for the kickoff:
- Confirm dataset / prompt templates to use for realistic token sizes.
- Confirm client-side keepalive / connection settings (we may need 30s ping).
- Confirm whether TLS termination / custom domains / VPC peering are required for the PoC.

Marissa
AM, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme-ai.com>, Elizabeth Tan <e.tan@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Feb 2028 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT + streaming SLOs — follow-up & next steps

Samir / Elizabeth —

Great — Fri 2/18 10:00 AM PST works. I’ve gone ahead and booked the kickoff and included a short agenda: 
1) Confirm PoC scope & success criteria (TTFT p95 < 400ms under 200 req/s bursts, 300 concurrent streams).
2) Review test data and prompt templates.
3) Assign owners and timeline (engineering + SRE + your PM).
4) Next steps for billing/PoC pricing (Aditya).

Dev / Marissa — please be prepared with the capacity estimate and proposed instance types.

Samir — I’ll send the calendar invite and upload the PoC test plan to the HubSpot deal record. I’ll also include the two attachments we referenced.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Aditya
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
